jailor.glance: Your prisoner knows they were jailed; Jailor chat does not normally show your player name.
jailor.youSee: The jail interface and private prisoner chat identify whom you jailed. An execution attempt and its actual outcome must be recorded separately.
jailor.theySee: The prisoner gets a jail notice and can speak to the anonymous Jailor. A death from execution is public later; jailing alone does not publicly reveal your identity.
jailor.claimCheck: A prisoner can confirm the jail, but not automatically the Jailor’s player name. Keep the same prisoner, conversation and execution outcome.
jailor.reportTemplate: Jailor N[night]: jailed [player] — [released / executed / execution failed].

marshal.glance: A Tribunal is a public event, not a private night result.
marshal.youSee: Your daytime control starts a Tribunal when permitted. The public trial sequence supplies the outcome; you receive no investigative check for merely being Marshal.
marshal.theySee: Everyone sees the Tribunal and its trial/voting changes. They can check whether the public event you claim actually happened.
marshal.claimCheck: A private will line cannot substitute for a real Tribunal. Report the day and executions that everyone can verify.
marshal.reportTemplate: Marshal D[day]: Tribunal [called / held] — [public trial outcomes].

mayor.glance: A real reveal publicly identifies the Mayor.
mayor.youSee: Revealing changes your public role display and vote power. A quiet night gives you no investigative result.
mayor.theySee: Everyone sees the reveal and can account for the extra votes. The reveal also changes which protection and targeting options apply.
mayor.claimCheck: Saying Mayor in chat is different from using Reveal. After a claimed reveal, the public role display and vote count must agree.

monarch.glance: The knight receives a Knighted effect; the extra vote can be observed.
monarch.youSee: Use the resulting knight status and actual action feedback to track successful Knights. A selection click alone is not proof a Knight resolved.
monarch.theySee: A successful recipient gets the Knighted effect and extra vote. The effect demonstrates knighting, rather than giving them a routine investigative report on you.
monarch.claimCheck: A recipient’s effect and voting power can test this claim. Do not promise a successful Knight after an interrupted action.
monarch.reportTemplate: Monarch N[night]: Knight [player] — [confirmed / failed]; living knights: [players].

prosecutor.glance: A prosecution is public and can be checked by the whole town.
prosecutor.youSee: The daytime prosecution control and its public resolution supply your evidence. There is no normal nightly investigation.
prosecutor.theySee: Everyone sees who is prosecuted and the resulting execution. Applicable Town penalties and remaining uses affect what can happen next.
prosecutor.claimCheck: Use the actual day, defendant and outcome. A written claim cannot create the public prosecution event.

coroner.glance: Your examined player does not receive your autopsy or killer-match result.
coroner.youSee: Autopsy establishes the relevant killer information. A later Examine gives a match or no-match against that autopsied killer; preserve the corpse and suspect separately.
coroner.theySee: The suspect does not receive your private comparison result. An observer may still see an ordinary Examine visit.
coroner.claimCheck: A killer match is not a universal evil check. State which corpse supplied the comparison, and record no autopsy or a failed Examine honestly.
coroner.reportTemplate: Coroner D[day]: Autopsy [corpse]. N[night]: Examine [player] — [match / no match / failed].

investigator.glance: Crimes are your private result; the checked player is not sent the same report.
investigator.youSee: The report concerns Murder on the checked night and Trespassing history. A failure or missing result is separate from No Crime.
investigator.theySee: Your subject does not receive a normal notice listing the crimes you found. Direct movement can still be observed by other roles.
investigator.claimCheck: Murder means an attack, not necessarily a death; Trespassing is not just tonight’s destination. Framing and concealment can alter the report.
investigator.reportTemplate: Investigator N[night]: [player] — [Murder / Trespassing / both / No Crime / failed].

lookout.glance: You get visitors to one house; those visitors do not receive your list.
lookout.youSee: A successful Watch lists observable players visiting the watched house, or no visible visitors. It does not list their destinations elsewhere.
lookout.theySee: The watched player and visitors do not receive your Lookout report. Astral or camouflaged movement can be absent from what you see.
lookout.claimCheck: Use the watched house and visible visitor list. No visible visitors does not prove that no astral ability affected the house.
lookout.reportTemplate: Lookout N[night]: watched [house] — visitors [players / none visible / failed].

psychic.glance: Only you receive the vision; the selected player is not sent your group.
psychic.youSee: A normal odd-night Good vision contains two players; an even-night Evil vision contains three. Keep the selected player in the group and retain any failed or unavailable result.
psychic.theySee: The selected player does not normally get a Psychic vision notice. Ordinary direct movement can still be seen by an observer.
psychic.claimCheck: The group guarantees at least one apparent Good or Evil player, not exactly one. Keep both/all three names; a secret exact-role read is not a Psychic result.
psychic.reportTemplate: Psychic N[night]: [Good: player, player / Evil: player, player, player] — selected [player]; [failure if any].

seer.glance: Friends or Enemies is your private comparison, not an exact-role reveal.
seer.youSee: A successful comparison returns Friends or Enemies for the chosen pair. A prevented action or invalid target is not a normal comparison result.
seer.theySee: Neither target receives your private comparison. Your two ordinary visits may be observed, subject to movement-changing effects.
seer.claimCheck: Friends does not necessarily mean two Townies, and Enemies does not identify which person is evil. Preserve the exact pair and any failure.

sheriff.glance: The checked player does not get your Innocent or Suspicious result.
sheriff.youSee: A successful Search reports Innocent or Suspicious. That is an appearance check; it does not identify the actual role or faction in every case.
sheriff.theySee: Your subject gets no routine Sheriff result notice. An observer may still see the direct Search visit.
sheriff.claimCheck: Keep the exact target and result. Innocent can include protected Coven appearances and Neutral Killings; an interrupted check is not Innocent.

messages.when: A successful Search returns an Innocent appearance
messages.text: You cannot find any evidence of wrongdoing. [Player] seems innocent.

messages.when: A successful Search returns a Suspicious appearance
messages.text: [Player] seems suspicious!

spy.glance: A bug can name an evil visiting role without naming the player who owns it.
spy.youSee: A placed bug waits for a qualifying event. Its trigger can identify evil activity or a role; an untriggered bug is not a clean bill of health.
spy.theySee: The bug report is private to you. It is not a universal visitor list delivered to the bugged player.
spy.claimCheck: Name the bug location and the actual reported activity. Do not turn a role label into a player number without separate evidence.
spy.reportTemplate: Spy N[night]: Bug [player] — [untriggered / exact reported event / failed].

tracker.glance: You get one player’s visible destinations; those destinations do not receive your tracking report.
tracker.youSee: A successful Track reports the subject’s observable destinations, or no visible visit. Some abilities can generate multiple destinations.
tracker.theySee: Your subject and their destinations do not normally get a message naming you as their Tracker. Your own direct visit can still be observed.
tracker.claimCheck: An astral action can return no visible visit. A destination report is not a Lookout list of everyone at that house.
tracker.reportTemplate: Tracker N[night]: tracked [player] — visited [destinations / nobody visible / failed].

bodyguard.glance: A real interception can notify the saved target and leave a public Bodyguard death.
bodyguard.youSee: A successful Guard can intercept an eligible direct attack and fight the attacker. A quiet target list supplies no save confirmation by itself.
bodyguard.theySee: A saved target can receive protection feedback. The attacker and any resulting deaths create other evidence; a quiet night does not prove an interception.
bodyguard.claimCheck: Keep Guard distinct from the one Self Protect. Do not claim a fight solely because the chosen target survived.
bodyguard.reportTemplate: Bodyguard N[night]: Guard [player] — [no interception reported / intercepted attack / failed].

cleric.glance: An attacked recipient can see a Barrier message; it does not name you as Cleric.
cleric.youSee: The Cleric receives an attack notice naming the protected player when that target is attacked. On an ordinary unblocked night with no attack, there is no special save notice: selecting Barrier is not itself an attack result. The notice does not identify the attacker or prove your Barrier alone caused survival.
cleric.theySee: The attacked, Barrier-protected recipient can receive the quoted Barrier notice. That is their message, not the visiting Cleric’s message about them. A blocked attacker may receive a defense notice. A quiet target is not evidence of a save.
cleric.claimCheck: Speak from the Cleric’s screen: an attack notice, no attack feedback, or the actual failure are different accounts. Other Barrier abilities produce the same recipient notice, and another protector may resolve the attack first. During Grace Period N1, do not claim an ordinary Barrier visit to another player.

messages.when: At night resolution when the protected target is attacked; another protector resolving first can still produce this notice. The player mention is replaced here
messages.text: [player name] was attacked last night!

messages.when: The attacked recipient sees this when a Barrier protects them. Do not describe this as your own notice about someone you visited; it can be your own screen only if you were the attacked, protected player
messages.text: You were attacked, but a Barrier protected you!

cleric.reportTemplate: Cleric N[night]: Barrier [player] — [no attack reported / attack reported / failed].

claimScenarios.title: Target attacked · attack notice received
claimScenarios.screen: The Cleric sees the named-player attack notice above. You can report receiving attack feedback; it gives no attacker identity. Bodyguard or Trapper may have handled the attack first, so this is not exclusive credit for a save.
claimScenarios.report: Cleric N[night]: Barrier [player] — got attack feedback.
claimScenarios.meaning: This claim says you received an attack notification about that target. It does not say the recipient’s Barrier message appeared on your screen.

claimScenarios.title: Quiet night · no attack notice
claimScenarios.screen: Normally no special attack/save message appears for the target. There is no sourced “nothing happened” message to quote. The target surviving alone does not turn this into a save.
claimScenarios.report: Cleric N[night]: Barrier [player] — no attack feedback.
claimScenarios.meaning: If asked what you saw: “No attack notification; I had Barrier on [player].” You are claiming an uneventful protection attempt, not a confirmed save.

claimScenarios.title: Action prevented · roleblock, jail or obstacle
claimScenarios.screen: Use the failure notice that actually applies, rather than a quiet-success account. An Unknown Obstacle prevents the normal remote attack feedback; the old bug that revealed it anyway was fixed in R1.5.03. Exact failure wording is not quoted here.
claimScenarios.meaning: If claiming roleblocked, say “I tried to Barrier [player], but I was roleblocked.” Do not also claim an ordinary completed visit or normal target-attack feedback.

claimScenarios.title: Target died · check the cause
claimScenarios.screen: An Unstoppable attack can defeat Barrier’s Powerful Defense. A death does not by itself prove the action was prevented. This is not a separate guaranteed “Barrier failed” message; keep any actual attack notice and the death outcome separate.
claimScenarios.report: Cleric N[night]: Barrier [player] — [attack feedback, if any]; target died.
claimScenarios.meaning: If arguing an Unstoppable attack, check the death evidence before giving that explanation. Do not invent a notification naming the attacker or its attack strength.

crusader.glance: A protected player can see Crusader protection; a visitor death can publicly name Crusader.
crusader.youSee: You can receive feedback that your protected target was attacked and that you attacked a visitor. These are different events, not the same player.
crusader.theySee: The protected resident can receive protection feedback. A visitor can be attacked, and a resulting public death can identify Crusader as the cause.
crusader.claimCheck: Fortify protects the resident and may attack one random direct visitor. Do not say you attacked the resident or choose a visitor identity that you were never given.

messages.when: A player dies to the Crusader attack, if the cause is not hidden
messages.text: they were killed by a Crusader

crusader.reportTemplate: Crusader N[night]: Fortify [player] — target [attack/no attack reported]; visitor [attack/no attack reported].

oracle.glance: An attacked protected role-holder can see a Barrier; observers see no ordinary Aegis visit.
oracle.youSee: Aegis targets a Town role, not a player number. Use actual attack feedback for protected role-holders; an enabled choice or a survivor alone is not save confirmation.
oracle.theySee: An attacked and protected recipient can see a Barrier message. Aegis is astral, so Tracker and Lookout do not see an ordinary Oracle visit; other players’ visits stay visible.
oracle.claimCheck: Name the selected Town role and follow consecutive-role/self-role restrictions. A generic Barrier notice does not prove an Oracle identity or hide your real role’s direct travel.
oracle.reportTemplate: Oracle N[night]: Aegis [Town role] — [no attack reported / attack reported / failed].

trapper.glance: A harmless trigger gives you roles; the resident is not normally told about that trigger.
trapper.youSee: Build completion and trap status are separate from a placed trap triggering. A non-harmful trigger can report visitor roles; attack handling has different feedback.
trapper.theySee: A resident is not routinely told that harmless visitors triggered a trap. A trap that prevents an attack can notify the saved player and leave attack/death evidence.
trapper.claimCheck: Record build, placement and trigger separately. Role order is not player order; trap information does not supply matching player numbers.
trapper.reportTemplate: Trapper N[night]: [Build / Place on player / trigger]; reported roles or attack: [actual feedback].

deputy.glance: A daytime shot is a public event, not a private investigation.
deputy.youSee: Your shot resolves in public, including any miss/defense outcome. The public event and any applicable penalty determine what you can do next.
deputy.theySee: Everyone can see the shot event and its target/outcome. A shot does not give you a hidden nightly result to post later.
deputy.claimCheck: An unperformed shot cannot be supplied by a copied will. Report the public target and outcome; check the current shot control and eligibility.
deputy.reportTemplate: Deputy D[day]: shot [player] — [public hit / defense or miss / other shown outcome].

trickster.glance: A successful absorption is separate from the later Unleash; quiet mirroring confirms no save.
trickster.youSee: A Magic Mirror can absorb one qualifying direct attack and tell you the stored attacker role. Unstoppable attacks shatter it rather than supplying a normal stored attack.
trickster.theySee: Other players can receive attack/protection evidence from the event. An Unleash can use the absorbed role’s death label, rather than a generic Trickster kill label.
trickster.claimCheck: Do not claim an absorption because the target survived. Record the supplied attacker role, keep the stored state, and separate Mirror from Unleash.
trickster.reportTemplate: Trickster N[night]: [Mirror player / Self Mirror / Unleash player] — [no absorption / reported attacker role / actual outcome].

veteran.glance: A visitor can receive a Veteran attack message; no report gives you a full visitor list.
veteran.youSee: Alert and resulting attack feedback concern visitors to your own house. An Alert alone is not a complete list of visitors or guaranteed kills.
veteran.theySee: Direct visitors can be attacked, and public deaths can identify Veteran as the cause. Astral visits and survival effects can change the outcome.
veteran.claimCheck: Keep the Alert night and actual attacks separate. Do not invent names for every visitor or claim a normal visit while staying home.
veteran.reportTemplate: Veteran N[night]: [Alert / no Alert] — [actual attack feedback or none].

vigilante.glance: A victim can see a Vigilante attack; defense means a shot need not produce a death.
vigilante.youSee: Load before shooting. Later shot feedback and any guilt/penalty are actual outcomes, not an alignment result inferred from whether somebody died.
vigilante.theySee: The target can receive an attack notice and public deaths can expose a Vigilante shot. Surviving a shot does not by itself tell you their faction.
vigilante.claimCheck: Preserve the bullet spent and outcome. Do not write an N1 shot while still loading, or label defense as a precise role.
vigilante.reportTemplate: Vigilante N[night]: [Load / hold / shoot player] — [actual hit / defense / failure feedback].

admirer.glance: Admire tests your Obsession; Bestow creates a lasting effect another player can check.
admirer.youSee: You begin with an Obsession subalignment clue. Admire tests a player; finding the Obsession unlocks limited Care. No valid Obsession can produce a distinct notice.
admirer.theySee: Care can give the Obsession Barrier feedback when attacked. Bestow grants lasting astral visits plus roleblock/control immunity; the recipient can check their effects and later ability behavior.
admirer.claimCheck: Use the current Obsession/Care/Bestow model. Do not invent old public proposals, acceptance/rejection scenes, or mutual exact-role reveals.

messages.when: No eligible secret Obsession remains
messages.text: There are no valid targets for your secret Obsession.

admirer.reportTemplate: Admirer N[night]: Admire [player] — [Obsession / not Obsession / failed]; Care [if unlocked]. D[day]: Bestow [player].

amnesiac.glance: A remembered role changes your own role card; it is not a nightly check on another player.
amnesiac.youSee: When Remember resolves, the new Town role and its controls replace Amnesiac. Record the change when it happens rather than predicting a role before resolution.
amnesiac.theySee: Other players do not automatically receive your complete private remembered-role history. Graveyard deaths and later role demonstrations can test your account.
amnesiac.claimCheck: Record the starting role and actual remembered role separately. Hidden or altered corpses and unique-role priority can affect what you obtain.
amnesiac.reportTemplate: Amnesiac D[day]: [no role remembered / remembered role] — first available action [if any].

retributionist.glance: The reanimated body supplies role-specific feedback; a missing corpse is not a negative check.
retributionist.youSee: Select a usable Town corpse and its destination. You can receive that corpse ability’s result or a corpse-use failure; preserve which body supplied it.
retributionist.theySee: Recipients may see the reanimated ability’s ordinary effect. That alone does not prove which living corpse-user produced it.
retributionist.claimCheck: A body being taken or unavailable is not an Innocent/no-match result. Keep body, destination, actual result and the Town-only corpse pool consistent.

messages.when: The chosen corpse is unavailable
messages.text: Your target's corpse is missing!

retributionist.reportTemplate: Retributionist N[night]: [Town corpse] → [destination] — [actual ability result / corpse unavailable / failed].

socialite.glance: Rejected visitors see an obstacle; you do not get a complete list of their identities.
socialite.youSee: Invitations and the Guest List determine who is admitted. A Party can tell you that someone was rejected, rather than furnishing a Lookout report.
socialite.theySee: Eligible uninvited visitors can get obstacle/failure feedback. Invited, astral and Party-immune actions do not all behave identically.
socialite.claimCheck: Record the invitation/Party and whether rejection was reported. Do not identify every rejected player from a simple rejection notification.
socialite.reportTemplate: Socialite D[day]: invited [player]. N[night]: [Party / no Party] — [rejection reported / none / failed].

tavern-keeper.glance: The recipient can see drink/roleblock feedback and may confirm or dispute the effect.
tavern-keeper.youSee: A completed Drink is distinct from an interrupted visit. Immunity and retaliation can change the result; a visit alone does not prove the target was roleblocked.
tavern-keeper.theySee: A target may receive a drink or roleblock/immunity notice. An uncautious Serial Killer can retaliate and leave a distinctive death explanation.
tavern-keeper.claimCheck: Keep Hangover and roleblock immunity in mind. Do not turn a failure to block into an exact-role identification.
tavern-keeper.reportTemplate: Tavern Keeper N[night]: Drink [player] — [completed / immune / failed / actual feedback].

catalyst.glance: An Overcharged player can test the extra action through their own controls.
catalyst.youSee: Your targeting and action feedback establish what you attempted. The recipient’s compatible ability determines how an extra action becomes available.
catalyst.theySee: The affected player can observe an Overcharge effect and additional permitted ability use. Timing and limitations depend on the ability and setup.
catalyst.claimCheck: Coordinate the recipient’s expected extra action instead of claiming a particular result for them. Extra destinations are not exclusive proof of Seer.

pilgrim.glance: You have no role ability that generates a nightly target result.
pilgrim.youSee: Your role card, public events and effects applied by others supply information. There is no Pilgrim investigation or protective action to resolve.
pilgrim.theySee: Others can observe public speech, votes and effects they cause to you. No private Pilgrim ability confirms their role or alignment.
pilgrim.claimCheck: A truthful history has no active visit or investigation. Do not turn being unharmed into a claimed mechanical check.
pilgrim.reportTemplate: Pilgrim N[night]: no active role ability. Public observations: [facts].

archmage.glance: A retrained ally sees a changed role card; this does not automatically change faction.
archmage.youSee: Retrain changes the eligible ally’s role and controls. With the book, the ordinary attack is an alternative to Retrain; record the mode that actually resolved.
archmage.theySee: The retrained player can observe their new role. Targets of a book attack can receive Coven attack feedback, with deaths public later.
archmage.claimCheck: Do not post private Retrain information as a Town-role result. A cover history must survive the new action and movement pattern.

hex-master.glance: A Hex is not a public exact-role announcement; the final bomb is public.
hex-master.youSee: Track Hex state and the final-condition progress from your own interface. A placed Hex is not an ordinary attack death.
hex-master.theySee: Hexed players need not announce a Hex for it to exist. At the final resolution, the town receives the Hex Bomb event and deaths.
hex-master.claimCheck: Do not use private Hex state as a supposed Town investigation. With the book, distinguish the astral Hex attack from ordinary travel.

messages.when: The Hex Bomb resolves
messages.text: The Town has been Hex Bombed!

witch.glance: A controlled player can receive a control notice and challenge an unrelated cover.
witch.youSee: Control has a first target and forced destination. The controlled role’s feedback can give private information; your own ordinary movement is to the first target.
witch.theySee: The controlled player can receive control or immunity feedback. Their forced action may generate messages/evidence at the second destination.
witch.claimCheck: A harmless one-target protection story does not explain a control complaint. Do not put your first target’s private role in an unrelated Town will.

conjurer.glance: Meteor is publicly visible; it cannot be quietly passed off as an ordinary night action.
conjurer.youSee: The daytime Meteor control and its public resolution provide the result. A book attack is a different nighttime action.
conjurer.theySee: Everyone sees the Meteor event and victim. The displayed death/event exposes Conjurer activity even if it does not identify every faction member.
conjurer.claimCheck: A cover must account for the public Meteor timing. Do not rewrite a daytime victim as a private Sheriff result or ordinary protective night.

messages.when: A Meteor resolves
messages.text: [Player] faces an untimely end!

ritualist.glance: A wrong ritual guess gives no replacement role result.
ritualist.youSee: Blood Ritual reports success or failure and spends an attempt. Failure does not tell you which different role the target holds.
ritualist.theySee: A successful ritual can leave distinctive attack/death evidence. With the book, ordinary attacks have a separate presentation and cannot occur as an independent second ritual.
ritualist.claimCheck: Do not fabricate an exact-role result from failure. Check eligible roles, illuminated status and the current attempt limit before acting.

jinx.glance: Other direct visitors can receive a private message with your name and the visited house.
jinx.youSee: You learn that you Jinxed a visitor of the chosen house. This does not give you every visitor’s player name or role, or prove the visitor died.
jinx.theySee: Direct co-visitors can see a message naming the Jinx and the shared destination. The attacked visitor is not a safe exception: a survivor can report you too. A Jinx death cause is public unless hidden by a setup effect.
jinx.claimCheck: A Crusader story cannot erase a witness’s Jinx message. A claimed Lookout list is also unsupported by simply knowing you attacked a visitor.

messages.when: At the end of a night visiting the Jinx’s chosen house
messages.text: You saw the Jinx [Jinx name] visit [target name]!

messages.when: A player dies to the Jinx attack, if the cause is not hidden
messages.text: They were killed by a Jinx.

dreamweaver.glance: The target can see Dreamweaver/Insomnia effects, while you do not receive their exact Town role.
dreamweaver.youSee: Your action and the target’s later state concern Dreamweave/Insomnia. They do not supply a Town role investigation.
dreamweaver.theySee: A qualifying target can see Dreamweave/Insomnia notices; a Town visit on the following night can prevent Insomnia. Insomnia and its removal change their available abilities.
dreamweaver.claimCheck: An ordinary protection story can conflict with the target’s status. Record cures and cleared effects; do not treat every applied status as permanent.

enchanter.glance: Your altered death information is what the public can read, not proof it was genuine.
enchanter.youSee: Track which player you Enchanted and any Alterate role/will you submitted. Framing is not an investigative discovery of their true role.
enchanter.theySee: Investigatives can receive altered appearances. On an Alterated death, the displayed role/will can be the forged version rather than the true one.
enchanter.claimCheck: Do not cite your own frame or forged will as independent confirmation. A corpse-user or other private result may contradict the public display.

illusionist.glance: A disguised death can show a chosen role; favorable investigation is not a faction change.
illusionist.youSee: Track the chosen Illusion, Phantasm or death Disguise separately. The role-changing display does not grant the claimed role’s actual abilities.
illusionist.theySee: Investigatives can receive altered appearances, and public death information can show a Disguise. These displays do not establish the player’s actual faction.
illusionist.claimCheck: A book attack is direct and replaces the ordinary protective choice. A nonvisiting cover must account for that switch in observed movement.

medusa.glance: The graveyard can hide role and will; Coven can still receive the real information.
medusa.youSee: Track your actual Stone marks and charges. A marked death can expose the true role/will privately to Coven while others see hidden information.
medusa.theySee: Stone is a persistent mark, not a protection notice. When a marked player dies, ordinary opponents can be denied the role and will; observers can still see a direct Stone visit.
medusa.claimCheck: A Cleric claim cannot explain a visible N1 protective visit during Grace Period. Privately readable Stoned information is not a Psychic or Sheriff result.

necromancer.glance: Recipients can see the corpse ability’s effect; that does not certify a Town corpse-user.
necromancer.youSee: The reanimated body can supply role-specific feedback. Record the body, destination and mode; a book attack is a separate action choice.
necromancer.theySee: Targets may receive the reanimated ability’s normal message or attack evidence. They do not thereby learn that a Town Retributionist produced it.
necromancer.claimCheck: A Ret cover has a smaller legal body pool. Evil/hidden bodies or private self-protection can expose a false Town-only corpse history.

poisoner.glance: Drink and Smog give different visible problems to affected players.
poisoner.youSee: Record Drink versus Smog and the action’s actual outcome. A Smog rejection is not a complete list of visitor identities.
poisoner.theySee: A Drink recipient can receive roleblock/immunity feedback. Eligible visitors encountering Smog can receive an obstacle; the resident need not get that same visitor message.
poisoner.claimCheck: Match the effect witnesses describe. A roleblock or obstacle complaint is not ordinary protection feedback; Hangover and immunity can also explain failures.

potion-master.glance: A Reveal gives you a private exact-role line; a Barrier recipient sees protection, not your identity.
potion-master.youSee: The selected potion determines the feedback: attack, protection, or an exact-role reveal. Keep the chosen mode and any failure separate.
potion-master.theySee: An attacked Barrier recipient can receive generic Barrier feedback. A Harmful potion can leave attack evidence; your Reveal report is private to you and informed allies as applicable.
potion-master.claimCheck: Do not present a private exact-role Reveal as a Sheriff/Seer result. A Barrier message alone does not uniquely prove Cleric or Oracle.

voodoo-master.glance: Silence, Deafen and Blind affect different parts of the recipient’s screen.
voodoo-master.youSee: Record the selected thread and actual outcome. The victim’s missing chat/results are not an exact-role result for you.
voodoo-master.theySee: Silence prevents speech, Deafen removes other players’ chat/whispers, and Blind suppresses nightly results. On an ordinary text-chat trial, a Silenced player can use the limited ellipsis response.
voodoo-master.claimCheck: A protection cover can conflict with the recipient’s status. Blind notification wording is inconsistent across references; do not promise a particular explanatory line.

messages.when: Silence takes effect / the player attempts to speak
messages.text: Your voice seems to be lost! You can't speak.

wildling.glance: Your private movement and whisper information is not automatically public.
wildling.youSee: Sensed travel and permitted whisper information can give real destinations or private conversations. Keep what you actually observed distinct from a complete role reveal.
wildling.theySee: Observed players do not receive your entire private log. Your direct Sense/book visit can still be visible to other observers.
wildling.claimCheck: Tracker/Lookout reporting must match what that Town role could see. Do not copy private whispers or unrelated movement into a public claimed result.

covenite.glance: Without the book, you have no personal nightly role-result ability.
covenite.youSee: Your Coven chat/team information is private faction information. With the Necronomicon, record the actual attack and any feedback.
covenite.theySee: A book target may receive Coven attack feedback. Other players do not receive a special Covenite investigation/protection result.
covenite.claimCheck: Separate no-book holds from book travel. An invented nightly investigation is not supplied by Covenite’s actual ability.

cultist.glance: The converted player can see their faction change while retaining their role.
cultist.youSee: Your permitted day Indoctrinate converts an eligible player. Keep conversion state and any later book attack separate.
cultist.theySee: The converted player receives the new faction/team context and keeps their role’s real ability. Earlier Town demonstrations can remain mechanically genuine.
cultist.claimCheck: A former Town confirmation does not prove current allegiance. Do not claim Indoctrinate itself was a Town investigation or a role swap.

baker.glance: A public Famine announcement identifies the transformation, not the player who transformed.
baker.youSee: Bread markers and living recipients track your progress. Your starting Bread is separate from the ordinary living recipients needed for transformation.
baker.theySee: Transformation announces Famine to the town. Bread/Starvation effects are different from an ordinary protective save; the announcement alone does not name your player.
baker.claimCheck: Do not turn Bread status into a Cleric save or a visitor report. After transformation, your history must switch from Feed to Famine’s current ability.

berserker.glance: Rampage feedback and public deaths are not a complete visitor list.
berserker.youSee: Record the attack mode, actual rampage feedback and kill-based progression. A selected house alone does not tell you all visitors or guarantee each death.
berserker.theySee: Victims can get attack/death feedback and public deaths show the relevant cause unless hidden. A War transformation is publicly announced.
berserker.claimCheck: Do not report kill progress as an investigative check. Once War arrives, follow its new two-target action rather than the earlier Berserker story.

plaguebearer.glance: Your infection markers are broader than a list of visitors to one house.
plaguebearer.youSee: The interface tracks infected players and fresh spread. Starting infections and repeated infected contacts are not fresh observer reports.
plaguebearer.theySee: A public Pestilence transformation announces that condition was met. It does not make your private infection map a public Lookout result.
plaguebearer.claimCheck: If using a movement cover, distinguish active Infect, passive spread and existing infection. An infection event alone does not assign a visitor to a numbered house.

soul-collector.glance: Your soul count is private; becoming Death is publicly announced.
soul-collector.youSee: Track your souls and actual Reap state. Reap frames an appearance and can affect later soul gain, but is not itself a kill.
soul-collector.theySee: Investigatives can see the altered appearance of a Reaped player. At the threshold, the public Death transformation gives the town urgent new information.
soul-collector.claimCheck: An astral Reap does not support a normal visiting cover. Keep private soul counts and invented exact-role findings out of public Town reports.

doomsayer.glance: Your success/failure line is private; a wrong set does not reveal which guess was wrong.
doomsayer.youSee: A correct set of three guesses produces success feedback. A failed set says at least one was wrong, without supplying a replacement list of roles.
doomsayer.theySee: A successful Doom creates the relevant deaths and your departure/win evidence. Other players do not get a routine list of your failed guesses.
doomsayer.claimCheck: Do not treat one failed triple as three cleared players. Keep the permitted guess categories and the actual night’s outcome separate.

messages.when: All three submitted role guesses are correct
messages.text: You have chosen wisely. All three roles are correct.

messages.when: At least one submitted role guess is wrong
messages.text: You have chosen poorly. At least one of your guesses is incorrect.

executioner.glance: A qualifying target execution produces public outcome evidence; private target assignment is yours.
executioner.youSee: Your assigned target and actual win/transform state establish progress. A death by another route is not automatically the qualifying execution.
executioner.theySee: The trial and any revenge/win/departure events can be seen publicly. They do not give other players your earlier private target-selection information.
executioner.claimCheck: A cover story must fit the public trial. If you become Jester, switch to Jester’s conditions instead of claiming the old target objective is still active.

jester.glance: The public revenge announcement can distinguish a qualifying hanging from an invalid one.
jester.youSee: The interface gives a daily Chatterbox requirement and progress. A qualifying execution and available Haunt are different from failing the quota or dying at night.
jester.theySee: The town sees the hanging and the appropriate revenge/no-revenge announcement. A later Haunt creates attack/death evidence.
jester.claimCheck: A role claim does not replace the quota or qualifying death condition. Preserve which voters and targets the client actually permits.

messages.when: A Jester with a completed Chatterbox is hanged
messages.text: The Jester will get their revenge from the grave!

messages.when: A Jester without a completed Chatterbox is hanged
messages.text: The Jester cannot be bothered getting revenge beyond the grave!

pirate.glance: Scour information concerns your Landlubbers; it is not a normal Sheriff result.
pirate.youSee: Your objective and Scour feedback concern the three Landlubbers. A Plunder is a separate attack action with limited charges and a real outcome.
pirate.theySee: A victim can receive Pirate attack/death feedback; public deaths can advance the objective even when you did not kill that player.
pirate.claimCheck: Use the current Scour/Plunder rules. Old duel choices and duel-result messages are not a valid current claim history.

arsonist.glance: Most victims do not get a routine Doused notice; another Arsonist can detect their own gasoline.
arsonist.youSee: Track active Douse, passive Douse from visitors and self-Doused state separately. Taking no action can Clean you; Ignite is a distinct action.
arsonist.theySee: A normal Douse is not a protection/save notice. Fire deaths create public evidence later, while observers may see direct Douse travel.
arsonist.claimCheck: A visiting cover can fit a direct Douse destination but has no real protection. Clean/astral Ignite can fit a nonvisiting story only if earlier observed travel also agrees.

serial-killer.glance: Roleblock retaliation can leave a different death explanation from your selected attack.
serial-killer.youSee: Your selected attack, Cautious setting and any passive retaliation are separate. Attack feedback is not an exact-role investigation.
serial-killer.theySee: Targets can get attack/death feedback. An uncautious roleblock retaliation can leave the distinctive roleblocker/jailed-SK explanation and affect their will.
serial-killer.claimCheck: Do not claim a clean ordinary visit account while ignoring retaliation. The person you chose to attack is not necessarily the only relevant victim.

messages.when: A Tavern Keeper or Poisoner gives you a drink
messages.text: Someone gave you a drink last night, but you have high tolerance.

shroud.glance: A shrouded player can appear to have attacked; death evidence alone does not identify their intent.
shroud.youSee: Record direct Attack versus Shroud and the action’s outcome. A failed shrouding route can result in a different direct attack path.
shroud.theySee: The forced attack can create Murder evidence on the shrouded player. The attacked recipient and public deaths can supply attack evidence without establishing a willing killer.
shroud.claimCheck: Keep your own destination and the forced attacker’s destination separate. A Seer/Tracker account must fit the movement it actually claims to observe.

werewolf.glance: A persistent Scent result does not mean you visited that player again tonight.
werewolf.youSee: Scent and Full Moon attacks give different information. An existing scent can keep supplying destinations without a fresh visit to that subject.
werewolf.theySee: Victims of a Full Moon attack/rampage can get attack feedback and leave public deaths. That does not broadcast your complete private scent history.
werewolf.claimCheck: A fresh Tracker account about an old scented player can conflict with your real attack elsewhere. Preserve the current moon and actual travel mode.

cursed-soul.glance: A successful role swap changes both role cards; it does not swap factions.
cursed-soul.youSee: After a successful Soul Swap, your new role and controls are the relevant actual state. An attempted swap alone does not prove success.
cursed-soul.theySee: The other player can observe their changed role. The retained faction context matters; a familiar Town ability can now belong to a different allegiance.
cursed-soul.claimCheck: Do not keep reporting the old role’s power after losing it. An old role read does not establish anyone’s current role or faction.

vampire.glance: A converted Town player keeps their real role ability and sees a new faction context.
vampire.youSee: Track Convert versus Drain and actual success. Defense or an ineligible faction can prevent a conversion; a button click is not confirmed recruitment.
vampire.theySee: A successfully converted player gets the Vampire faction/team context while retaining the role. Drain and succession create different outcomes.
vampire.claimCheck: A genuine Town-role demonstration can remain genuine after conversion. Avoid the obsolete youngest-biter account and distinguish conversion from a kill.

famine.glance: Opponents can suffer starvation effects; transformation did not instantly kill everyone.
famine.youSee: You now use Starve and Bread depletion, rather than Baker’s earlier Feed plan. Record the current controls and actual living Bread state.
famine.theySee: The town has seen the Famine announcement. Starvation and later deaths create evidence, but that announcement does not identify which numbered player is Famine.
famine.claimCheck: A prior Baker-style history must stop claiming fresh Feed actions. Your current Starve action supplies neither a Town save nor an investigative result.

messages.when: Baker transforms into Famine
messages.text: The Baker has transformed into Famine, Horseman of the Apocalypse! A famine has begun!

war.glance: The town knows War exists; victims can receive Unstoppable rampage evidence.
war.youSee: You can select up to two distinct Rampage targets. Actual deaths and feedback establish outcomes; a chosen target is not a full list of visitors.
war.theySee: The public transformation announces War without directly identifying the player. Rampage deaths and attack feedback create new public/private evidence afterward.
war.claimCheck: Do not continue a one-target Berserker buildup or invent investigative results from your kill count. Account for both real destinations when choosing a cover.

messages.when: Berserker transforms into War
messages.text: The Berserker has transformed into War, Horseman of the Apocalypse!

pestilence.glance: Stack effects and lethal Pestilence outcomes differ from ordinary attack-defense feedback.
pestilence.youSee: Your current Spread Pestilence and stack state replace the old infection-completion task. Record actual applied stacks/outcomes rather than an old passive-rampage result.
pestilence.theySee: The public transformation announces Pestilence. Affected players can experience stack effects and lethal outcomes; this is not a standard protection message.
pestilence.claimCheck: Do not claim the old ToS1 Pestilence rampage or a fresh Plaguebearer infection log. Use the transformed ability and check current client feedback.

messages.when: Plaguebearer transforms into Pestilence
messages.text: A Plague has consumed the Town, transforming the Plaguebearer into Pestilence, Horseman of the Apocalypse!

death.glance: The Death announcement is public; your immediate objective is surviving the day.
death.youSee: Your transformation and current-day survival replace Soul Collector’s next-night Reap progression. Check the actual end-of-day resolution.
death.theySee: The town sees Death’s arrival and can act before its resolution. A subsequent apocalypse event is public rather than a private attack result you can reinterpret.
death.claimCheck: Do not continue a Soul Collector count/visit story as though transformation never happened. A normal protective or investigative report cannot manufacture the end-of-day event.

messages.when: The end-of-day Death event resolves
messages.text: Death has claimed the souls of the Town!
